Ahitub
ă-hī'tŭb
n. (a priestly name of the house of Eli and afterwards of the house of Zadok — standing at the hinge where one priestly line was cut off and another established)
From Hebrew 'Achituwb, “my brother is goodness” or “brother of goodness”, from 'ach, brother, and tob, good. At least two and probably three priests bear it.

Biblical Definition

Ahitub is a name that sits exactly on the fault line of the Old Testament priesthood. The first Ahitub is of the doomed house: “Ahiah, the son of Ahitub, Ichabod's brother, the son of Phinehas, the son of Eli” (1Sa 14:3) — grandson of Eli, nephew of the child born the day the ark was taken. His son Ahimelech gave David the shewbread and Goliath's sword at Nob, and for it Doeg the Edomite informed on him — “I saw the son of Jesse coming to Nob, to Ahimelech the son of Ahitub” (1Sa 22:9) — and Saul had eighty-five priests killed in a day, which fulfilled the word spoken against Eli's house. Only Abiathar escaped. The second Ahitub is of the house that replaced it: “Zadok the son of Ahitub, and Ahimelech the son of Abiathar, were the priests” (2Sa 8:17), and the Chronicler traces the descent plainly — “Ahitub begat Zadok, and Zadok begat Ahimaaz” (1Ch 6:8). Zadok stayed with David when Absalom rose and with Solomon when Adonijah rose; Abiathar did not, and was thrust out from being priest, “that he might fulfil the word of the LORD which he spake concerning the house of Eli in Shiloh”. One name, two houses, and a warning between them.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) has no article for Ahitub; in sacred history the name belongs to a grandson of Eli and to the father of Zadok the priest.

expand to see more

AHITUB, n. The son of Phinehas and grandson of Eli, high priest of the line of Ithamar.

The name signifies brother of goodness.

His son Ahimelech was slain by Doeg at the command of Saul, with fourscore and five priests of Nob.

Another Ahitub, of the line of Eleazar, was the father of Zadok, who was made priest in the room of Abiathar.

In him the high priesthood returned from the house of Ithamar to the house of Eleazar.

Key Scripture

1Sa 22:9 — "Then answered Doeg the Edomite, which was set over the servants of Saul, and said, I saw the son of Jesse coming to Nob, to Ahimelech the son of Ahitub."

2Sa 8:17 — "And Zadok the son of Ahitub, and Ahimelech the son of Abiathar, were the priests; and Seraiah was the scribe;"

1Ch 6:8 — "And Ahitub begat Zadok, and Zadok begat Ahimaaz,"

1Sa 2:31 — "Behold, the days come, that I will cut off thine arm, and the arm of thy father's house, that there shall not be an old man in thine house."

Modern Corruption

Sacred office is treated as a possession secured by ordination and lineage; the house of Eli held both and was cut off, because God's word to it turned on how its sons behaved.

expand to see more

The house of Eli had everything an office can give. It held the high priesthood, the ark was in its keeping at Shiloh, and the succession was hereditary and unquestioned. What it did not have was sons who feared God: Hophni and Phinehas took the flesh by force and lay with the women at the door of the tabernacle, and their father restrained them with words and no more. The sentence is one of the most searching in Scripture — “them that honour me I will honour, and they that despise me shall be lightly esteemed” (1Sa 2:30). It was executed in stages: the ark taken, Eli dead at the gate, the slaughter of the priests at Nob under Saul, and finally Abiathar deposed by Solomon. Ordination secures nothing. A minister's standing is not his credentials, and a church's continuance is not its charter.

The second matter is Doeg, because he is the mechanism. He was “detained before the LORD” at Nob on the day David came — present at the sanctuary, observing worship, and taking notes for the king. The informer is a permanent figure in the church's history, and Psa 52, written about this incident, describes him exactly: a tongue devising mischiefs like a sharp razor, a man who “trusted in the abundance of his riches” rather than in God. That psalm ends where the priesthood ended up: “I am like a green olive tree in the house of God: I trust in the mercy of God for ever and ever.”

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew 'Achituwb (H285), from 'ach (H251), brother, and tob (H2896), good; Tsadoq (H6659), Zadok, righteous.

expand to see more

Hebrew 'Achituwb (H285) — Ahitub, “my brother is goodness”; borne in both priestly houses.

Hebrew tob (H2896) — good; the word of Gen 1, and the second element of the name.

Hebrew Tsadoq (H6659) — Zadok, “righteous”; his son, from whom the Zadokite priesthood descends.

Hebrew 'Ebyathar (H54) — Abiathar, “the father of abundance”; the last priest of Eli's line.

Hebrew Nob (H5011) — Nob, the priests' city where the tabernacle stood and where they were slain.

Usage

"“Ahimelech the son of Ahitub” — the priest Doeg informed against."

"“Zadok the son of Ahitub” — the house that took the office."

"“Ahitub begat Zadok” — the line that held the sanctuary to the exile."
